review.summary: I found 6 issues in the WP18 queue and integration code: 3 MAJOR and 3 MINOR. I did not review or certify the source-reader internals. These things look right: tenant scoping on the delivery id and log key; the per-submission lock and the uniqueness check, which together stop duplicate deliveries; the retry receipt written after a failed transaction, which keeps completed receipts; and send-time unavailability, which now goes to the outbox retry instead of being marked superseded. The main risks are: (1) Some candidates never get a receipt, so they stay first in the batch order forever and can block every batch. (2) The materializer and send-time check are tied to one exact report id. Ordinary report turnover may then permanently skip or supersede recipients who still qualify. (3) If the snapshot passed to the send-time check lacks the idempotency key or recipient hash, every completed follow-up is silently superseded. An empty or partial findings list does not certify that tests pass or that this is ready to release.

findings.area: processDueCompletedFollowups: candidate ORDER BY tried NULLS FIRST + 'invalid_snapshot' / 'claimed_elsewhere' branches
findings.issue: Head-of-line starvation. Some candidates come back on every run but never get an AutomationExecutionLog receipt, so `tried` stays NULL and they keep sorting first. This happens when completedFollowupDeliveryKey/Id throws (e.g. registration submissionId is NULL or not an Identity), or when the FormSubmission lock finds no row (submission deleted, or FormSubmission.liveId differs from the registration's liveId). These rows stay first and can fill the whole LIMIT on every tick.
findings.evidence: The 'invalid_snapshot' path does `results.push(...); continue;` with no log write. `if (locked.length!==1) return "claimed_elsewhere"` also writes nothing. The SQL keeps rows with `attempt.id IS NULL` and sorts `tried NULLS FIRST`. A NULL g."submissionId" gives a NULL sha256 key, so the attempt join and the EmailDelivery NOT EXISTS check both keep the row.
findings.impact: If `limit` (default 50) or more such orphan or invalid rows exist within the 7-day window, no real completed follow-up is ever materialized for any tenant. Fewer of them still waste batch capacity on every tick.
findings.recommended_fix: Filter out unusable rows in SQL: `g."submissionId" IS NOT NULL`, an Identity regex on the ids, and an EXISTS check on a FormSubmission with a matching id and liveId. For rows that still fail in application code, write a terminal 'skipped' receipt with an invalid_snapshot error code. Write nothing only when the lock was truly skipped because another transaction holds it; to tell these cases apart, check for row existence without SKIP LOCKED.
findings.required_test: Seed limit+1 completion rows whose registration has a NULL or missing FormSubmission, plus one valid eligible row. Run processDueCompletedFollowups twice with limit=limit. Assert the valid row is queued and the invalid rows get a terminal receipt or are excluded.

findings.area: ineligible branch in processDueCompletedFollowups; isCurrentCompletedFollowupDelivery reportId binding via idempotencyKey
findings.issue: The queue code cannot tell 'recipient no longer qualifies' apart from 'the referenced report/rule snapshot is no longer current'. Both come back as 'ineligible'. The materializer then writes a permanent 'skipped' receipt, and the send-time check finalizes the delivery as config_superseded. Report ids change often: any new registration or order changes the input revision and creates a new report. Reports also expire. So a recipient who still qualifies can permanently lose the follow-up if the report changes between candidate selection and the transaction, or before a retried send (SMTP retries come after a backoff). The SQL also chooses the newest of possibly several current ready reports (DISTINCT ON ... r."createdAt" DESC). That choice may differ from the report the reader's current-ready gate picks.
findings.evidence: `if(source.status==="ineligible") { ...upsert status:"skipped"... return "superseded" }`. The delivery key embeds `reportId`. At send time, `source.status==="eligible"` must hold for that exact reportId, otherwise `finalizeSuperseded(..., "config_superseded")`. The SQL candidate gate requires `r."inputRegistrationRevision"=wp20_metric_registration_revision(...)`, which shows reports go stale whenever registrations change.
findings.impact: Follow-ups that should be sent are silently and permanently dropped under normal live traffic. Retries are the most exposed, because they run after reports have turned over.
findings.recommended_fix: Change the source-reader contract (as a separate scope) so that 'report/rule reference no longer current' is a distinct result from 'recipient ineligible'. Treat the stale-reference result as retryable or unavailable: do not write a terminal 'skipped' receipt. At send time, recheck eligibility against the current report for the same (vendor, live, submission, rule), not the exact reportId stored in the key. Alternatively, document and test that the reader resolves the current report itself and uses reportId only as a lower bound.
findings.required_test: (a) Select a candidate, then create a newer ready report before the transaction runs. Assert that no 'skipped' receipt is written and that a later run queues the delivery. (b) Queue a delivery, refresh the report, and fail the first SMTP attempt. Assert the retry still sends and is not finalized as config_superseded.

findings.issue: isCurrentCompletedFollowupDelivery returns false (meaning superseded) when `idempotencyKey` or `recipientHash` is missing. Its parameter declares both fields as optional, so the compiler cannot ensure the claimed-delivery snapshot actually selects them. The diff does not add idempotencyKey to EmailDeliverySnapshotIdentity or to the claim select. The function also returns false when the recipient hash is not exactly 43 base64url characters, which is an assumption about createEmailRecipientHash's output format.
findings.evidence: Signature: `idempotencyKey?: string; recipientHash?: string`. The checks are `(delivery.idempotencyKey ?? "").split(":")` and `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/u.test(delivery.recipientHash ?? "")`. The email-delivery.ts hunks only change the database type, not the identity Pick or the claim select.
findings.impact: If either field is not loaded, or the hash format differs, every completed follow-up is finalized as config_superseded and never sent. Nothing fails loudly.
findings.recommended_fix: Make idempotencyKey and recipientHash required in the parameter type, and make sure EmailDeliverySnapshotIdentity and the claim query select both. Validate the hash by comparing it with createEmailRecipientHash output, not a hard-coded length.
findings.required_test: End-to-end test: materialize an eligible completed follow-up, then run processDueEmailDeliveries with the real claim path and a stubbed transport. Assert status 'sent' and that sendTransactionalEmail was called once.

findings.issue: Every error other than P2002 is recorded as 'completed_source_unavailable' and retried every 5 minutes with no attempt cap until the 7-day window closes. This includes programming errors, payload-encryption key/config failures from protectEmailDeliveryPayload, and invalid data that throws inside the reader.
findings.evidence: `catch(error) { if P2002 ...; ... create:{...status:"failed",errorCode:"completed_source_unavailable"} ... updateMany ... startedAt:now }`. The candidate SQL re-selects failed rows after RETRY_MS, with no attempt count.
findings.impact: Persistent failures look like source outages. Each affected row costs a transaction and a monitoring event every 5 minutes for up to 7 days.
findings.recommended_fix: Retry only FollowupSourceUnavailableError and transient Prisma errors such as P2034 or connection errors. Record any other error with a distinct error code, and add an attempt counter or cap.
findings.required_test: Make protectEmailDeliveryPayload throw a non-availability error. Assert the receipt's errorCode differs from completed_source_unavailable and that retries stop after the cap.

findings.area: completedFollowupDeliveryId: idempotency scope is (vendor, live, submission)
findings.issue: Deduplication is per submission, not per recipient. If the same email address registered twice for one live (resubmission), with two registrations that both complete, it gets two separate marketing follow-ups. The reader's same-email check only covers orders, not earlier follow-up deliveries.
findings.evidence: The delivery id hashes `vendorId\nliveId\nsubmissionId`. Nothing checks for an existing EmailDelivery with the same recipientHash and the trigger completed_followup for the same live.
findings.impact: Duplicate marketing email to one person, which raises complaint and unsubscribe risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Inside the RR transaction, after the source read, skip (with a receipt) when an EmailDelivery already exists with the same vendorId, sourceLiveId, trigger=completed_followup and recipientHash. Alternatively, derive the idempotency key from the recipient hash.
findings.required_test: Two submissions with the same email for one live, both completed. Assert exactly one queued completed_followup delivery.

findings.area: candidate SQL (CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements + per-row wp20_* revision functions)
findings.issue: Every job tick runs this query across all tenants. It expands every completion row of every ready report and runs the revision functions plus a lateral rule lookup and an anti-join for each, all before LIMIT. Nothing restricts it to recent reports or to tenants with a matching active rule first.
findings.evidence: There is no early filter on vendors with an active `viewer_completed` rule and no index-driven bound on r."createdAt". The LIMIT applies only after DISTINCT ON over the full expansion.
findings.impact: Job latency grows with total completion volume. Because the route runs this before processDueEmailDeliveries, a slow query delays existing transactional and auth email in the same invocation.
findings.recommended_fix: Filter first on vendors that have a qualifying active rule, and on reports with "expiresAt" > now and a recent createdAt. Evaluate the revision functions once per report in a CTE. Consider a statement timeout for this query.
findings.required_test: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the producer-PG fixture with a realistic number of reports and completion rows. Assert a bounded runtime and that the email job still runs processDueEmailDeliveries within its budget.
